name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis; BRIEF ratifies the /spec:mocks approved set) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each `--via loop`; /spec:design, /spec:build, and /spec:review remain each stage's direct entry, spec-build-driver.js and spec-review-driver.js stepped: admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros, and verdict derived by verdict.js, with test-author dispatch, per-wave worker dispatch, repair, reviewer dispatch, and dispositions held by the session) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.98.0 — the kit: shared primitives named before any screen (brief 22a): `/spec:mocks` gains a `KIT` state between `SHAPES` and `WIREFRAMES` that writes `design/kit/<name>.html`, a canon family sibling to `design/shell/` under the same marks and the same checker, signed off on the page via `stop open kit` / `--mark kit-signed`; once a kit family resolves, every content region of a labeled mock carries `data-kit="<key>"` or `data-bespoke="<key>: <difference>"` naming the primitive it is not and why, `check` prints a running kit/bespoke count per screen plus an unabsorbed total (informational, never a violation), and `journey-approved` refuses on an unmarked region; `--reopen kit` clears the kit sign-off and the terminal approval only. A host with no `design/kit/` is unaffected byte-for-byte. 7.97.0 — sketch owns high fidelity and closes with a fixed critique pass (brief 22a): `/spec:sketch`'s scoped sweep now authors every gap surface at production fidelity in the picked theme and reworks the brief's existing gray mocks into it (the one re-authoring exception), and its loop writes a three-line UX argument (`job:`/`risk:`/`choice:`) into the brief's `surfaces` block per surface touched; a new fixed step runs `check --states`, `render-gate --mocks`, and one fresh-context `design-critic` (Opus, read-only) dispatch on the four blind spots (error prevention · error recovery · help · efficiency) before every exit stop, recording findings as page notes (`notes add --by critic --reason <blindspot>`); `design-atlas.js check` gains two stamp-bound violations — a labeled mock still linking `wire/` once `design/tokens.css` exists (violation at `ratified`, warn at `sketch`, `approved` wireframes exempt) and a `ratified` mock with unresolved critic/human notes on its own label — both byte-identical no-ops when their store is absent; `mocks-notes.js`'s reason enum gains the four blind spots and `notes add`/`notes open` carry them. 7.96.0 — gray states on every wireframe (brief 22a): `design-atlas.js check --states` requires every labeled non-canon mock to declare `data-state-btn` switches for `empty`, `loading`, and `error` alongside the happy path, or opt one out with `data-no-state="<name>[,<name>]"` on the labeled root naming a product reason recorded as a ledger row; `mocks-driver.js` runs the check at `journey-drawn` and `journey-approved`, refusing the mark with the missing states named and the remedy to redraw them; `render-gate --mocks` captures every declared state as before, so the empty/loading/error frames join the render matrix with no gate change; the mocks-driver test fixture's `writeWireframe` now draws all three states by default.
